name: Nuke Egg
imitates: A drifting trout or salmon egg: a translucent foam ball with a milky yarn veil; best when spawning fish are upstream.
recipe: Conventional egg yarn, white or pale pink

steps.text: Start the thread behind the eye and build a thread base to mid-shank, leaving the thread hanging about a quarter shank back from the eye.
Pull a pencil-diameter clump of McFlyFoam (for a #16) and tie it on top of the shank with three tight turns, one directly over the other.
Pull both ends of the foam up and trim them straight across; the distance between shank and scissors sets the egg size.
After trimming, the foam is a rough tuft that is not yet round.
Fluff the foam with your fingers into a loose ball. You can stop here for a plain egg or continue to make a Nuke Egg.
Bring the thread in front of the egg, clip a short piece of egg yarn, peel off a few fibers and drape them around the egg as a sparse, ragged veil.
Pinch the yarn down behind the eye, twisting a little so it spreads around the hook, and make two tight thread turns over the veil.
Use a dubbing brush to comb the front-facing yarn back over the egg without pulling it all to the top.
Make several tight turns of thread just behind the eye to build a small wedge that holds the yarn back.
Whip finish and clip the thread. The finished fly.
